title: Independence of experts
subject: This guide addresses the requirement that an expert providing a report under the Corporations Act must be independent of the commissioning party and other interested parties. It covers the principles and factors ASIC considers when assessing independence, including relationships, interests, and the need for a genuine opinion.
background: The guide is issued under ASIC's powers to administer the Corporations Act 2001, particularly provisions requiring expert reports in contexts such as takeovers, schemes of arrangement, and related party transactions. It is intended for experts who prepare reports, as well as any person who commissions, issues, or uses an expert report, to clarify ASIC's interpretation of the independence requirement.
ruling: ASIC interprets the independence requirement strictly, requiring that an expert must not have any relationship or interest that could reasonably be seen as impairing its ability to provide an objective and unbiased opinion. The guide sets out factors ASIC will consider, such as financial interests, business relationships, and prior involvement with the commissioning party. ASIC expects experts to disclose all relevant relationships and interests, and if independence cannot be maintained, the expert should decline the engagement. The guide also addresses the use of specialists and the need for the expert to take responsibility for the report's content.
